name: demo_i4_pipes
source: [AS] assumed generic 2.0 L naturally-aspirated I4 for tools/ps_engine_audio's demo/listening test (ps_audio A10). NOT a real engine - every geometry/table value is a plausible, unmeasured [AS] guess, deliberately mirroring tests/support/cycle_fixtures.h's generic fixture geometry (bore/stroke/valves/lift) and tests/support/cycle_pipe_fixtures.h's generic pipe geometry (intake runners/plenum, exhaust primaries/merge tree), so this file's own map-generation cost/behaviour matches what those tests already exercise. cycle.resolution is not set: the live audio path uses the ResolutionCycleDesc default audio dx (0.032 m exhaust / 0.017 m intake). ps_audio A10 had doubled it to 0.064/0.034 m to avoid a NaN blow-up about 0.9 s after a WOT hold closed; ps_audio A8b traced that to a CFL violation, not to this file: at valve overlap under the near-vacuum overrun manifold the cylinder blows a supersonic (Mach ~2, |u|+a ~1260 m/s) backflow jet into the intake runner, beyond the build-time CFL check's assumed intake wave speed (500 m/s), and the explicit update diverged. PipeNetwork now sub-cycles a pipe whose runtime CFL exceeds the limit (tests/unit/test_pipe_network.cpp P9, tests/unit/test_engine_rig_audio.cpp A8b B1), so the default dx is stable. idle_pipes task (2026-09-29, car_sedan_pipes.json's idle hunt, root-caused via a per-tick trace of PowertrainDebug/EngineSoundState - see test_car_sedan_pipes.cpp's header comment for the measured before/after bands): two combined causes, both fixed - (1) grid_rpm did not cover idle_rpm (800; started at 1000), so every low-rpm lookup including the idle feed-forward bisection used Table2D's edge-clamped 1000 rpm row; grid_rpm now starts at 800.0, the lowest node the offline generator could actually converge at (trim_tolerance 0.02) - 250 rpm/30 kPa failed 'not settled, mean plenum 41255.9 Pa' (37.5% over target), 500 rpm/30 kPa failed 'not settled, mean plenum 30796.1 Pa' (2.65% over, just outside tolerance) even after fix (2) below, confirming this floor is a structural settling-time limitation of the offline generator at low rpm, not a throttle-leak artifact; both dropped, no owner-requested lower node (~200 rpm, ~500 rpm) is reachable for this cycle geometry. (2) even with 800 rpm covered, throttle_body.area_fraction_vs_position's closed-throttle (x=0) leak fraction (was 0.01, 1% of bore area) was too large: at 800 rpm even a fully closed throttle produced positive net torque (measured net(0) = +46.99 Nm via engine_simulated.cpp's idle_ff bisection), so no idle equilibrium existed at all and the bisection degenerated to ff=0. Reduced to 0.002 (0.2% of bore area), which gives net(0) = -11.93 Nm and a valid idle_ff solution (idle_p_im ~= 29.5 kPa, close to the 30 kPa grid node). Residual: the idle PI still hunts in a bounded, non-growing limit cycle (was ~1040-1280 rpm, now ~759-1301 rpm sustained - much closer to true idle) - confirmed independent of DFCO (disabling it widened the oscillation) and of simple PI gain scaling (a 10x gain cut left a similar-magnitude oscillation), so this is a structural idle-loop issue (the idle PI's own d(theta_idle)/d(omega) is not in the implicit solve's d, a documented CLAUDE.md backlog item), not force-tuned here.

cycle.source: [AS] assumed generic cycle-model inputs, not measured - mirrors tests/support/cycle_fixtures.h::make_generic_i4_cycle_desc() (geometry/valves/lift/friction) and tests/support/cycle_pipe_fixtures.h::make_pipe_i4_cycle_desc() (pipe geometry). No real engine's cited data was used. grid_rpm extended to start at 800 (was 1000) by the idle_pipes task (2026-09-29) so the generated maps cover idle_rpm - see this file's top-level 'source' field for the full writeup (why 250/500 rpm nodes are unreachable, and the paired throttle_body leak-area fix).
